name: Enoxaparin
status: PILOT – † lines checked against package insert 2026-11-15; awaiting review
dagger_note: † = general pharmacology; not in the SA guideline and not stated in the package insert consulted
item_format: t=text, s=source:printed page (s=pi: package insert), d=dagger, n=from own notes, b=bold, h=heading
summary: Subcutaneous anticoagulant for prevention and treatment of venous thrombo-embolism and for acute coronary syndromes.

forms.t: Pre-filled syringes 20 mg, 40 mg, 60 mg, 80 mg, 100 mg (100 mg/mL); 300 mg multidose vial (contains benzyl alcohol – not for neonates)

moa.t: Low molecular weight heparin with more anti-factor Xa than anti-factor IIa (thrombin) activity
Longer duration of action than unfractionated heparin; weight-adjusted dosing

pk.t: Anti-Xa half-life 4.5 hours (6.7 hours in the elderly); activity gone within 24 hours of a dose
Clearance falls with creatinine clearance; exposure about 65% higher when creatinine clearance < 30 mL/minute
Peak anti-Xa effect 3–5 hours after SC injection

dosing.h: VTE prophylaxis in pregnancy and puerperium

items.t: < 100 kg: 40 mg SC daily; ≥ 100 kg: 60 mg SC daily
Post-partum prophylaxis: start 6–12 hours after delivery
1 mg/kg SC 12 hourly OR 1.5 mg/kg SC daily
Overlap heparin with warfarin for at least 5 days
1 mg/kg SC 12 hourly for a minimum of 2 days

dosing.h: STEMI – adjunct after alteplase (not after streptokinase)

items.t: Loading: 30 mg IV bolus, then 1 mg/kg SC as a single dose (total cumulative dose not above 100 mg)
Maintenance: 1.5 mg/kg SC daily or 1 mg/kg SC 12 hourly, until angiography or for the hospital stay, max 8 days
> 75 years: omit the IV loading dose; loading 0.75 mg/kg SC as a single dose

administration.t: Deep SC injection into the abdominal wall with the patient lying down, alternating left and right; do not rub the site
Do not expel the air bubble from the 20 mg and 40 mg pre-filled syringes

adjustments.t: eGFR < 30 mL/minute: prophylaxis 20 mg daily; treatment 1 mg/kg daily
Morbid obesity: individualise dosing in discussion with a specialist
Women < 45 kg and men < 57 kg: higher exposure and bleeding risk at fixed prophylactic doses – monitor closely
Used for VTE prophylaxis and treatment in pregnancy; skin reactions are more common in pregnant women – check the injection site
Not recommended in pregnant women with mechanical prosthetic heart valves

contraindications.t: Active major bleeding or high risk of uncontrolled haemorrhage, including recent haemorrhagic stroke
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia within the past 100 days, or circulating antibodies
Hypersensitivity to enoxaparin, heparin or other low molecular weight heparins
Use prophylaxis only exceptionally with: severe liver disease, peptic ulcer disease, intraocular / intracranial / spinal surgery, coagulopathy, uncontrolled hypertension

cautions.t: Lumbar puncture or spinal / epidural: not within 12 hours of a prophylactic dose or 24 hours of a therapeutic dose
Creatinine clearance < 30 mL/minute: consider doubling these intervals; delay the next dose at least 4 hours after catheter removal
Do not use heparins after streptokinase

adverse_effects.t: Haemorrhage is the most common reaction, including major and fatal bleeding
Thrombocytopenia (common); heparin-induced thrombocytopenia usually appears between days 5 and 21
Raised transaminases (very common); hyperkalaemia, skin necrosis at the injection site, osteoporosis after more than 3 months (all rare)

monitoring.t: Platelet count before starting and regularly during treatment; stop if platelets fall 30–50% from baseline
Anti-Xa monitoring is not routinely required; standard clotting tests are not suitable

toxicity.t: Bleeding: slow IV protamine partly neutralises the effect (anti-Xa activity at most about 60%); do not exceed 50 mg protamine per dose

conflicts.t: Children: the package insert states safety and efficacy are not established; the Paediatric STG gives a treatment dose.
Breastfeeding: the SA package insert says mothers receiving enoxaparin should not breastfeed; the STG gives post-partum prophylaxis without this restriction.
Own notes record that enoxaparin does not cross the placenta; the package insert says safety in pregnancy is not established and to use only when clearly needed.
